headline: High: Chatwoot’s broad egress and customer-data handling can leak or misroute support data when paired with Great Expectations’ file-based validation workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest messages and reports, and Great Expectations reads files such as data sources and documentation. If Chatwoot output is copied into validation artifacts or shared files, prompt-like content could influence downstream interpretation. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from the profiles.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are pasted into Great Expectations documentation or validation files
IF both agents share a writable workspace or clipboard bridge
mitigations: Use a separate folder for validation artifacts and support transcripts
Strip instructions from copied support text before saving
Require human review of any text imported from Chatwoot
Disable any shared clipboard or sync tool between the two workflows

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, and messages, while Great Expectations reads files and stores validation results. A shared workspace or copied files could expose customer data to validation artifacts. Great Expectations has no network egress, which lowers exfiltration risk, but the shared-file pathway remains plausible.
conditions: IF customer records are written into files that Great Expectations reads
IF validation results are stored in the same directory as support exports
mitigations: Keep customer exports out of the validation workspace
Redact identifiers before running validations
Store validation outputs in a separate directory
Restrict file permissions on shared folders
requires-engineering: add automated data-class filtering before file handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and API integrations, while Great Expectations can install packages and operates on files. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is limited. Any conflict would require an unusual shared target not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or repository
IF an operator gives both agents the same mutable OAuth-backed resource
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Use one-way export from Chatwoot to Great Expectations
Check for overlapping credentials before running both

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports, and Great Expectations can consume files and emit validation results. If Great Expectations treats Chatwoot-derived content as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect data-quality conclusions. The profiles do not show an explicit verification step, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes Chatwoot exports without a human verification step
IF validation rules are generated directly from Chatwoot text
mitigations: Require manual review of imported fields
Validate schema before content-based checks
Keep Chatwoot text separate from rule definitions
Add a second reviewer for any derived assertions

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and messages, while Great Expectations stores validation results and documentation. If regulated customer data is exported from Chatwoot into Great Expectations files, retention and residency policies can diverge. No specific certifications are documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is included in Great Expectations validation files
IF retention settings differ between Chatwoot exports and Great Expectations outputs
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from validation datasets
Align retention periods for exported files
Document the data flow between systems
Delete stale validation artifacts on a schedule
